conviction_note: Nagarro is a takeover stub, not an earnings stock: Persistent's EUR 81.00 cash offer is done (94.04% held after the additional acceptance period, closing guided for end-Q1 CY27, delisting and a squeeze-out planned), spot is EUR 78.80, a 2.8% spread, and the stock has traded EUR 77.0-79.8 since August on 20-day realised vol of 9.7% annualised. A Q3 quarterly statement cannot change the EUR 81 floor that a delisting offer or squeeze-out sets. The only thing in the release that could move it is a closing or regulatory update, which would narrow the spread. So the move is small (abs 1.0), with a slight lean up (p_up 52). The one finding (+0.2) and the scaled number (+0.04) agree in sign. The gap between them is just the low certainty.

already_public.what: Persistent (via Galaxy Germany Holding SE) EUR 81.00 cash takeover offer succeeded at 83.25% after the main acceptance period. Additional acceptance period 23 Sep - 6 Oct 2026. Closing expected by end-Q1 CY27, subject to 'a limited number of outstanding regulatory approvals'. Delisting intended.
Persistent holds 94.04% after the offer closed and plans a squeeze-out. No terms or dates given.
Offer terms: EUR 81 cash; Persistent does not plan a DPLTA for two years after closing; delisting from the regulated market after completion
Q2/H1 2026 results: revenue EUR 252.4m in Q2 (+2.0% in constant currency), adjusted EBITDA margin 15.0%. The release gives no explicit FY guide.

new_in_release.expect: Q3 2026 revenue and margins: unknown. Irrelevant to the price, which is anchored to the EUR 81 offer.
A possible update on regulatory approvals, closing timing, delisting or squeeze-out steps. If one comes it narrows the spread to EUR 81 (up). Absent one, nothing changes.
Unlikely to matter. A company being taken private has no guide the price trades on.

findings.finding: Nagarro trades as a takeover stub: EUR 81.00 cash offer completed at 94.04%, spot EUR 78.80 (2.8% spread), closing guided by end-Q1 CY27, delisting and squeeze-out planned. A Q3 statement cannot lower the EUR 81 floor. The only in-release item that can move the price is a regulatory, closing or squeeze-out update, and that would narrow the spread. So the print's expected effect is small and slightly positive.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Since the offer, the stock has held EUR 77.0-79.8 (Yahoo daily closes, Aug-Nov 2026). The Q2 release on 2026-08-14, inside the offer period, did not take it out of that band, and the cadence history shows -0.26% around the August print. Before the bid this name moved 22.8% and 29.7% on prints; that regime is over.
findings.original_quote: Persistent hält nach Abschluss des Übernahmeangebots 94,04 Prozent der Nagarro-Anteile. (goldesel.de, 09.10.2026) -- 'Persistent holds 94.04% of Nagarro's shares after the takeover offer closed'
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced. The 2.8% spread is the market's price for time to closing (about 4.5 months), the remaining regulatory risk and the squeeze-out timing. If the market expected the release to carry a closing update, spot would sit nearer EUR 80-81; it sits at 78.80, unchanged in the 5 days around the print. The small positive is the chance that the statement carries an approval update.
findings.independence: Same fact, different source: Persistent holds 94.04% and plans a squeeze-out (https://goldesel.de/aktien/news/nagarro-aktie-persistent-plant-squeeze-out-nach-ubernahme-von-9404-prozent). The offer terms are in the 2026-08-06 EQS release.

outside_window.finding: Regulatory clearances (two jurisdictions reportedly outstanding) and closing by end-Q1 CY27. On closing, the spread to EUR 81 collapses (+2.8%), unless the deal breaks (back toward the pre-bid ~EUR 34).

A squeeze-out or delisting offer, whose cash compensation must be at least the highest price paid (EUR 81). A merger squeeze-out compensation could be set above that by valuation, with a Spruchverfahren on top.
